previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with multiple myeloma, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, type 2 diabetes, chronic hemolytic anemia, and heart failure, was admitted for fever and confusion following an elotuzumab infusion. His symptoms were attributed to an infusion-related reaction, with no evidence of active infection on blood or urine cultures. He was treated with a course of antibiotics as a precaution and monitored closely. His encephalopathy resolved, and he remained afebrile by discharge. He had stable vital signs, improved kidney function, and no active bleeding despite persistent anemia and thrombocytopenia. Aspirin was held due to low platelets, and pomalidomide was paused pending oncology follow-up. He completed dialysis during admission, remained on fidaxomicin for C. difficile colitis, and was discharged to extended care rehab with clear mental status and a plan for close outpatient follow-up.

portal venous phase. Reformatted coronal and sagittal images through the

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis dated ___.  CT chest abdomen

FINDINGS: 

CHEST:

HEART AND VASCULATURE: Assessment is somewhat limited by motion but pulmonary
vasculature is moderately well opacified to the subsegmental level without
filling defect to indicate a pulmonary embolus.  The main, right and left
pulmonary arteries are enlarged, measuring 4.3 cm, 2.7 cm and 2.5 cm
respectively, suggestive of pulmonary arterial hypertension.  The thoracic
aorta is normal in caliber without evidence of dissection or intramural
hematoma.  The heart is enlarged.  There is a trace pericardial effusion,
likely within physiologic range.

AXILLA, HILA, AND MEDIASTINUM: No axillary, mediastinal, or hilar
lymphadenopathy is present.  No mediastinal mass.

PLEURAL SPACES: No pleural effusion or pneumothorax.

LUNGS/AIRWAYS: There is mild ground-glass and consolidative opacity at the
posterior aspect of the right upper lobe.  Evaluation of the lower lobes is
limited due to respiratory motion.  There is bilateral dependent atelectasis,
with possible additional ground-glass and consolidative opacity in the right
lower lobe.  The airways are patent to the level of the segmental bronchi
bilaterally.

BASE OF NECK: Visualized portions of the base of the neck show no abnormality.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout.  A
subcentimeter hypodensity in VI is too small to characterize by CT.  There is
no evidence of intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The
gallbladder contains gallstones without wall thickening or surrounding
inflammation.

PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without pancreatic
ductal dilatation.  A subcentimeter hypodensity in the head of the pancreas is
nonspecific, possibly representing an IPMN (11:44).  There is no
peripancreatic stranding.

SPLEEN: The spleen is enlarged, measuring 16.2 cm.  There is normal
attenuation throughout, without evidence of focal lesions.

ADRENALS: There is a 1.2 cm left adrenal nodule, which is consistent with an
adrenal adenoma on prior study.  The right adrenal gland is normal in size and
shape.

URINARY: The kidneys are mildly atrophic bilaterally.  There is no evidence of
focal renal lesions or hydronephrosis.  There is a 1.4 cm cyst arising from
the upper pole of the right kidney and a 1.6 cm cyst arising from the lower
pole of the right kidney.  There is no perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL: The stomach is unremarkable.  Small bowel loops demonstrate
normal caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement throughout.  Diverticulosis of
the colon is noted, without evidence of wall thickening and fat stranding.  A
large amount of stool is noted within the rectum, though evaluation for wall
thickening and stranding is limited by streak artifact from left hip
prosthesis.  The appendix is normal.  There is no free intraperitoneal fluid
or free air.

PELVIS:
Evaluation is limited due to streak artifact from left hip prosthesis.

The urinary bladder is decompressed and obscured by streak artifact..  There
is no free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: The prostate and seminal vesicles are grossly
unremarkable.

LYMPH NODES: There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There

atelectasis.  The moderate left pleural effusion has increased in size from
the previous study.  No pneumothorax.

LUNG:

1. PARENCHYMA: Ground-glass opacities of the right upper lobe have improved. 
A right lower lobe consolidation appears unchanged.  The left lower lobe
consolidation appears to have progressed from the prior study.
2. AIRWAYS:  The airways are patent to the level of the segmental bronchi
bilaterally.

CHEST CAGE: The bones are diffusely demineralized.  Diffuse, heterogeneous

of the thoracic vertebral bodies appear stable.  A compression deformity or
Schmorl's node of the inferior endplate of T1 is unchanged.  A lucency within
the manubrium appears stable.

IMPRESSION:

worsening infection, and a now moderate left pleural effusion, possibly
parapneumonic in etiology.
2. Stable right lower lobe consolidation and trace right pleural effusion. 
Interval improvement in right upper lobe ground-glass opacities.
3. Diffusely heterogeneous appearance of the axial skeleton, which may reflect
myelomatous involvement.  Multiple lucencies of the thoracic vertebral bodies
and sternum appear stable compared to the most recent prior CTA.
4. Stable dilatation of the main pulmonary artery, suggestive of pulmonary
hypertension.
5. Cholelithiasis.
6. Moderate splenomegaly.

performed with gradient echo, FLAIR, diffusion, and T2 technique were then
obtained.

COMPARISON  Noncontrast CT head from ___ and CTA of the head and
neck from ___

FINDINGS: 

The study is partly degraded by motion artifact.

There is no evidence of hemorrhage, edema, masses, mass effect, midline shift
or infarction.
Susceptibility artifact in the bilateral globi pallidi correspond to
calcifications on the CT.

 There are scattered T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in the cerebral hemispheres
bilaterally, a nonspecific finding and likely related to chronic small vessel
ischemic changes.

There is generalized parenchymal volume loss, most likely age related but
slightly more than expected for patient's age.  Prominence of the ventricular
system and extra-axial CSF spaces is consistent with the previously mentioned
parenchymal volume loss.

There is mild mucosal thickening along the ethmoid air cells.  A small mucous
retention cyst is seen in the right maxillary sinus.  There is near complete
opacification of the right mastoid air cells.  The left mastoid air cells
appear clear.

IMPRESSION:


1. No significant intracranial abnormality.  No evidence of acute infarction,
hemorrhage or mass.  No suspicious FLAIR signal abnormality.
2. Scattered white matter changes in the cerebral hemispheres bilaterally,
likely sequela of chronic small vessel ischemic changes.
3. Generalized parenchymal volume loss, slightly more than expected for
patient's age.
4. Paranasal sinus disease and near complete right mastoid air cell
opacification.
